source.author: verg
source.text: Paulatim adnabam terrae; iam tuta tenebam, ni gens crudelis madida cum veste gravatum prensantemque uncis manibus capita aspera montis ferro invasisset, praedamque ignara putasset.
source.text_original: Paulatim adnabam terrae; iam tuta tenebam, / ni gens crudelis madida cum veste gravatum / prensantemque uncis manibus capita aspera montis / ferro invasisset, praedamque ignara putasset.
source.text_english: Little by little I was swimming toward land; I was already holding safe ground, had not the cruel people, with their drenched clothing, attacked me as I clung to the rough heights of the mountain, gripping them with hooked hands, and thought me booty, unaware, because of my weapon.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: At subitus curaque ducem metus acrior omni mensque mali praesaga quatit, quod regis adortus progeniem raptoque dolis crudelis Acasto cetera nuda neci medioque in crimine patrem liquerit ac nullis inopem vallaverit armis, ipse procul nunc tuta tenens; ruat omnis in illum quippe furor.
reuse.text_original: At subitus curaque ducem metus acrior omni / mensque mali praesaga quatit, quod regis adortus / progeniem raptoque dolis crudelis Acasto / cetera nuda neci medioque in crimine patrem / liquerit ac nullis inopem vallaverit armis, / ipse procul nunc tuta tenens; ruat omnis in illum / quippe furor.
reuse.text_english: But a sudden and more piercing fear than any concern shakes the leader’s mind, foreboding evil: that, after attacking the king’s offspring and, by fraud and violence, cruelly snatching Acasto, he has left the rest exposed to death and, in the midst of their peril, abandoned their father, and has not ringed the defenseless man with any arms, while he himself now remains far away in safety; surely let all their fury fall upon him.
